description: The bar chart illustrates the performance, measured by MAP@10, of two sampling strategies—labeled as “Uniform Sampling Strategy” (yellow bars) and an unnamed purple strategy—across five values of the parameter *m* (6, 7, 8, 9, and 10). The vertical axis (MAP@10) ranges from 23.0 to 27.0, with major gridlines at 0.5 intervals. The horizontal axis displays the parameter *m*, with the purple bars on the left and the yellow bars on the right for each *m* value, suggesting a side-by-side comparison. The purple strategy consistently outperforms the uniform sampling strategy across all *m* values, with MAP@10 scores ranging from approximately 25.95 (*m*=6) to 26.8 (*m*=7), while the uniform strategy scores range from roughly 24.4 (*m*=6) to 25.6 (*m*=8). The highest performance is achieved by the purple strategy at *m*=7, and the lowest by the uniform strategy at *m*=6 and *m*=10. The chart includes a legend in the upper right, identifying the purple bars with no explicit label and the yellow bars as “Uniform Sampling Strategy.” No error bars or statistical annotations are visible, and the bars are not sorted by height but are ordered by increasing *m*.
